newsitem.title: USA: Oregon Senate sends suicide measure back to voters.
newsitem.headline: Oregon Senate sends suicide measure back to voters.

text.p: Oregon voters, who in 1994 made the state the first to legalise physician-assisted suicide, will get to take a second look at the issue in November.
The state Senate voted 20-10 Monday to hold a second referendum on the issue Nov. 4, following House approval.

Democratic Gov. John Kitzhaber, a physician, opposes the assisted-suicide law but also opposed the plan to send the measure back to the voters, who approved the original referendum by a 52-48 percent margin.
Kitzhaber, however, cannot veto the legislature's decision.

Oregon's pioneering law allows physicians to prescribe a lethal dose of pills to patients who make a properly witnessed request after receiving two opinions that they have less than six months to live.
The law was blocked by litigation shortly before it was to go into effect, although a federal appeals court this year tossed out the legal challenges.

Observers are waiting for a Supreme Court ruling on the controversial issue, expected within the next several weeks. In January the court heard arguments on state laws banning assisted suicide in Washington and New York that have been challenged by right-to-die proponents.
